h: שַׁבָּת הַגָּדוֹל, מַאֲמָר ד׳ Shabbos HaGadol — Maamar Daled
Avadim Hayinu Until "To Atone": Peh Sach and the Chosen House

p: בְּשֻׁלְחָן עָרוּךְ אוֹרַח חַיִּים
In Shulchan Aruch Orach Chaim
(סִימָן ת"ל):
(Siman 430):
וְנוֹהֲגִין לוֹמַר מִתְּחִילַּת עֲבָדִים הָיִינוּ עַד לְכַפֵּר עַל כָּל עֲוֹנוֹתֵינוּ.
"And it is customary to recite from the beginning of 'Avadim Hayinu' until 'to atone for all our iniquities.'"
הָעִנְיָן: אַף שֶׁיֵּשׁ מִצְוַת זְכִירַת יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם בְּכָל יוֹם,
The explanation is: although there is a mitzvah to remember the Exodus from Egypt every day,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם לְסַפֵּר בַּאֲרִיכוּת וְשֶׁיִּהְיֶה "כָּל הַמַּרְבֶּה לְסַפֵּר הֲרֵי זֶה מְשׁוּבָּח" לֹא מָצִינוּ רַק בְּפֶסַח,
nevertheless, to recount it at length such that "whoever elaborates in recounting is praiseworthy" we find only on Pesach;
וּמַה טִיבוֹ לְשַׁבָּת הַגָּדוֹל?
so what is its connection to Shabbos HaGadol?
אַךְ בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
However, in the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק ב' מ"ז:)
אִיתָא:
it is stated:
וּבְשַׁבָּת בְּמִילֵּי דִּשְׁמַיָּא וּבִקְדוּשָּׁה דְּיוֹמָא בָּעוֹ לְאִתְּעָרָא.
"And on Shabbos, one must awaken [holiness] with heavenly matters and with the holiness of the day."
קְדוּשָּׁה דְּיוֹמָא הַיְינוּ קְדוּשָּׁה הַמְּיוּחֶדֶת לְשַׁבָּת זוֹ,
"The holiness of the day" means the holiness unique to that specific Shabbos,
שֶׁכָּל שַׁבָּת יֵשׁ לוֹ קְדוּשָּׁה מְיוּחֶדֶת,
for every Shabbos has a unique holiness,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
as it is said
(בְּמִדְבַּר כ"ח, י'):
(Bamidbar 28:10):
עֹלַת שַׁבַּת בְּשַׁבַּתּוֹ,
"The burnt-offering of each Shabbos on its own Shabbos,"
וְכֵן כְּתִיב
and similarly it is written
(יְשַׁעְיָה ס"ו, כ"ג):
(Yeshayahu 66:23):
וְהָיָה מִדֵּי חֹדֶשׁ בְּחָדְשׁוֹ וּמִדֵּי שַׁבָּת בְּשַׁבַּתּוֹ
"And it shall be from new moon to new moon, and from Shabbos to its Shabbos"
שֶׁכָּל רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ יֵשׁ לוֹ קְדוּשָּׁה מְיוּחֶדֶת לְאוֹתוֹ חֹדֶשׁ,
for every Rosh Chodesh has a holiness unique to that month,
וְכֵן כָּל שַׁבָּת יֵשׁ לוֹ קְדוּשָּׁה מְיוּחֶדֶת לְאוֹתוֹ שַׁבָּת
and likewise every Shabbos has a holiness unique to that Shabbos
(וְנִתְבָּאֵר כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים).
(as has been explained many times).
וּכְבָר אָמַרְנוּ בְּמַה שֶּׁאוֹמְרִים: בֵּרַכְתּוֹ מִכָּל הַיָּמִים וְקִדַּשְׁתּוֹ מִכָּל הַזְּמַנִּים,
And we have already said regarding what we recite, "You blessed it above all days and sanctified it above all seasons,"
דְּשַׁבָּת כּוֹלֵל כָּל הַקְּדוּשּׁוֹת שֶׁיָּבוֹאוּ בְּשֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה שֶׁאַחֲרָיו,
that Shabbos includes all the holinesses that will come during the six weekdays following it,
וְשַׁבָּת מְקוֹר הַבְּרָכָה שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ יוּשְׁפַּע קְדוּשָּׁה וּבְרָכָה לְשֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה.
and Shabbos is the source of blessing from which holiness and blessing flow to the six weekdays.
וּקְדוּשַּׁת חַג הַפֶּסַח: פֶּה סָח,
And the holiness of the festival of Pesach is Peh Sach ("a mouth that speaks"),
וְכֵן כָּל קְדוּשַּׁת חֹדֶשׁ נִיסָן בִּכְלָל הוּא גַּם כֵּן מֵעִנְיָן זֶה,
and indeed the entire holiness of the month of Nisan in general also shares this theme,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסֵפֶר יְצִירָה
as they said in Sefer Yetzirah
(Chapter 5):
הִמְלִיךְ אוֹת ה' בְּשִׂיחָה וְכוּלֵּי וְנִיסָן בַּשָּׁנָה
"He made the letter Hei king in speech, etc., and Nisan in the year"
(וְנִתְבָּאֵר בְּרֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ נִיסָן),
(as explained in Rosh Chodesh Nisan),
וּבוֹ בָּא קְדוּשַּׁת חַג הַפֶּסַח פֶּה סָח.
and in it comes the holiness of Pesach, Peh Sach.
לָכֵן בָּא בּוֹ מִצְוַת סִיפּוּר יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם וְכָל הַמַּרְבֶּה לְסַפֵּר הֲרֵי זֶה מְשׁוּבָּח.
Therefore, in it comes the mitzvah of recounting the Exodus from Egypt, and "whoever elaborates in recounting is praiseworthy."
וּבְשַׁבָּת שֶׁקּוֹדֶם לוֹ שֶׁכּוֹלֵל קְדוּשָּׁתוֹ מַתְחִיל הַקְּדוּשָּׁה פֶּה סָח,
And on the Shabbos preceding it, which encompasses its holiness, the holiness of Peh Sach begins,
וְנוֹהֲגִין לוֹמַר מִתְּחִילַּת עֲבָדִים הָיִינוּ וְכוּלֵּי.
and it is customary to recite from the beginning of "Avadim Hayinu," etc.
אַךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמַר לְשׁוֹן "עַד לְכַפֵּר וְכוּלֵּי"
However, as to why it specifies "until 'to atone, etc.,'"
וְלֹא אָמַר עַד "רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר",
and did not say until "Rabban Gamliel says,"
כִּלְשׁוֹן הַגְּמָרָא
like the phrasing of the Gemara
(פְּסָחִים קי"ז.)
(Pesachim 117a)
עַד "בְּצֵאת יִשְׂרָאֵל", וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים עַד "לֹא לָנוּ"
"until 'When Israel went forth,' and Beis Hillel say until 'Not to us'"
הָעִנְיָן הוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאוֹמְרִים:
the explanation is based on what we say:
כַּמָּה מַעֲלוֹת טוֹבוֹת וְכוּלֵּי אִילּוּ הִכְנִיסָנוּ לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל וְכוּלֵּי עַל אַחַת כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה טוֹבָה כְּפוּלָה וּמְכוּפֶּלֶת וְכוּלֵּי
"How many degrees of goodness, etc.; had He brought us into the Land of Israel, etc.; how much more so, doubled and redoubled goodness, etc.,
וְהִכְנִיסָנוּ לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל וּבָנָה לָנוּ אֶת בֵּית הַבְּחִירָה לְכַפֵּר עַל כָּל עֲוֹנוֹתֵינוּ.
that He brought us into the Land of Israel and built for us the Chosen House to atone for all our iniquities."
וְיֵשׁ לְהָבִין מַהוּ הַטּוֹבָה הַבָּאָה לָנוּ הַיּוֹם מִבִּנְיַן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ אַחַר כִּי גָּלִינוּ מֵאַרְצֵנוּ וְנוּטַל כָּבוֹד מִבֵּית חַיֵּינוּ?
And one must understand: what benefit comes to us today from the building of the Holy Temple after we have been exiled from our land and glory has been taken from the House of our Life?
גַּם לְשׁוֹן "לְכַפֵּר עַל כָּל עֲוֹנוֹתֵינוּ" קָשֶׁה,
Also, the wording "to atone for all our iniquities (avonos)" is difficult,
דְּהָא רוֹב הַקָּרְבָּנוֹת מְכַפְּרִין עַל הַשּׁוֹגֵג וְלֹא עַל עָוֹן, דְּעָוֹן הַיְינוּ מֵזִיד,
for most sacrifices atone only for unintentional sins (shogeg) and not for avon, as avon means intentional sin (meizid),
כִּדְאִיתָא בְּיוֹמָא
as is stated in Yoma
וַהֲוָה לֵיהּ לוֹמַר "לְכַפֵּר עַל כָּל חַטֹּאתֵינוּ"!
so it should have said "to atone for all our inadvertent sins (chatos)"!
אַךְ כְּבָר אָמַרְנוּ דְּשַׁבָּת בַּזְּמַן כְּמוֹ מִקְדָּשׁ בַּמָּקוֹם,
However, we have already stated that Shabbos in time is like the Temple in space,
וּבְשַׁבָּת פְּרִיסַת סוּכַּת שָׁלוֹם עָלֵינוּ וְעַל כָּל עַמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל וְעַל יְרוּשָׁלָיִם,
and on Shabbos there is the spreading of the Shelter of Peace over us, over all His people Israel, and over Jerusalem,
שֶׁזּוֹכִין בְּשַׁבָּת לִקְדוּשַּׁת יְרוּשָׁלַיִם וּקְדוּשַּׁת הַמִּקְדָּשׁ הַנִּקְרָא סוּכַּת שָׁלוֹם.
for on Shabbos we merit the holiness of Jerusalem and the holiness of the Temple, which is called the Shelter of Peace.
וְהוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ
And this is based on what they said in the Midrash
(בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה י"א, ז'):
(Bereishis Rabbah 11:7):
יַעֲקֹב שֶׁכָּתוּב בּוֹ שְׁמִירַת שַׁבָּת נִיתַּן לוֹ הָעוֹלָם שֶׁלֹּא בְּמִדָּה,
"Yaakov, regarding whom observance of Shabbos is written, was given the world without measure,"
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא
as they said in the Gemara
(שַׁבָּת קי"ח.):
(Shabbos 118a):
כָּל הַמְּעַנֵּג אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת נוֹתְנִין לוֹ נַחֲלָה בְּלִי מְצָרִים וְכוּלֵּי: נַחֲלַת יַעֲקֹב אָבִיךָ.
"Whoever delights in the Shabbos is given an inheritance without boundaries, etc.: 'the inheritance of Yaakov your father.'"
דְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ נִתְבַּשֵּׂר רַק: לְזַרְעֲךָ אֶתֵּן הָאֲרָצוֹת הָאֵל
For our father Avraham was promised only, "To your seed I will give these lands"
אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל,
the Land of Israel,
וְכֵן בְּיִצְחָק נֶאֱמַר: גּוּר בָּאָרֶץ הַזֹּאת;
and similarly regarding Yitzchak it is said, "Sojourn in this land";
וְיַעֲקֹב זָכָה שֶׁבְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁיָּבוֹא יִזְכֶּה לִקְדוּשַּׁת אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל,
whereas Yaakov merited that wherever he goes he merits the holiness of the Land of Israel,
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר לוֹ: וּפָרַצְתָּ יָמָּה וְגוֹמֵר.
and this is what was said to him: "And you shall spread out westward, etc."
וּבַגְּמָרָא
And in the Gemara
(בְּרָכוֹת ל"ג.):
(Berachos 33a):
כָּל אָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ דֵּעָה כְּאִילּוּ נִבְנָה בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ בְּיָמָיו.
"Any person who has knowledge (da'as), it is as if the Holy Temple were built in his days."
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה הָאָדָם מִשְׁכָּן לַה',
That is, the person becomes a sanctuary for Hashem,
וְכָל אֶחָד לְפִי מַדְרֵגָתוֹ זוֹכֶה בְּשַׁבָּת לִקְדוּשַּׁת הַמָּקוֹם:
and each person according to his level merits on Shabbos the holiness of that sacred place:
יֵשׁ שֶׁזּוֹכֶה לִקְדוּשַּׁת מַחֲנֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל,
there is one who merits the holiness of the Camp of Israel,
וְיֵשׁ שֶׁזּוֹכֶה שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה לִבּוֹ קָדְשֵׁי הַקֳּדָשִׁים
and there is one who merits that his heart becomes the Holy of Holies
(וְנִתְבָּאֵר בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר בַּאֲרִיכוּת).
(as has been explained elsewhere at length).
וּבַתִּיקּוּנִים
And in Tikkunei Zohar
(תִּיקּוּן מ"ח)
(Tikkun 48)
אִיתָא עַל מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר
it is stated regarding what is said
(שְׁמוֹת ל"א, ט"ז):
(Shemos 31:16):
וְשָׁמְרוּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת לַעֲשׂוֹת אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת
"And the Children of Israel shall observe the Shabbos, to make the Shabbos"
תְּרֵין זִימְנִין אִדְּכַר הָכָא שַׁבָּת,
"Shabbos" is mentioned twice here,
לָקֳבֵל שְׁכִינְתָּא עִילָּאָה וְתַתָּאָה
corresponding to the Upper Shechinah and the Lower Shechinah,
וְהַיְינוּ ה' עִילָּאָה וְתַתָּאָה, שַׁבָּת עִילָּאָה שַׁבָּת תַּתָּאָה.
which are the upper Hei and lower Hei, Supernal Shabbos and Lower Shabbos.
וּמַסִּיק בְּתִיקּוּנֵי זֹהַר:
And Tikkunei Zohar concludes:
מַאי "לְדֹרֹתָם"?
"What is 'l'dorosam' (for their generations)?
זַכָּאָה אִיהוּ מַאן דְּעָבֵיד לוֹן דִּירָה בְּשַׁבָּת בִּתְרֵי בָּתֵּי לִיבָּא,
Fortunate is he who makes a dwelling (dirah) for them on Shabbos in the two chambers of the heart,
וְאִתְפְּנֵי יֵצֶר הָרָע מִתַּמָּן.
so that the evil inclination is cleared out from there."
וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁמּוּבָא
And this is along the lines of what is brought
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק א' קל"ח. בְּמִדְרָשׁ הַנֶּעֱלָם):
(Zohar, Vol. 1, 138a, in Midrash HaNe'elam):
לֹא יָרֵעוּ וְלֹא יַשְׁחִיתוּ בְּכָל הַר קָדְשִׁי
"They shall neither harm nor destroy in all My holy mountain"
דָּא לִיבָּא, דִּמְדוֹרֵיהּ דְּיֵצֶר הָרָע תַּמָּן,
this refers to the heart, for the dwelling of the evil inclination is there
שֶׁהַלֵּב נַעֲשָׂה הַר קָדְשִׁי, הַיְינוּ בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ,
so that the heart becomes "My holy mountain," meaning the Holy Temple,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
as it is said
(יְשַׁעְיָה נ"ו, ז'):
(Yeshayahu 56:7):
וַהֲבִיאוֹתִים אֶל הַר קָדְשִׁי.
"And I will bring them to My holy mountain."
וּבְשַׁבָּת שֶׁזּוֹכִין עַל יְדֵי קְדוּשַּׁת הַשָּׁלֹשׁ סְעוּדּוֹת לִבְחִינַת הַדַּעַת, קְדוּשַּׁת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ
And on Shabbos, when through the holiness of the three meals one merits the aspect of Da'as, the holiness of our father Yaakov
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב' י"ד:):
(as they said, Zohar, Vol. 2, 14b:
עֲבִיד לְיַעֲקֹב בְּרָזָא דְּדַעַת),
"He made Yaakov in the secret of Da'as"),
וְשַׁבָּת: ש' רָזָא דִּתְלַת אֲבָהָן וּבַת מִתְעַטְּרָא בְּהוּ
and Shabbos is Shin, the secret of the three Patriarchs, with Bas crowned by them
(ibid. 204a),
וְאָז כְּאִילּוּ נִבְנָה בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ בְּיָמָיו, שֶׁזּוֹכֶה שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה לִבּוֹ הַר קָדְשִׁי.
then it is as if the Holy Temple were built in his days, for he merits that his heart becomes "My holy mountain."
וְזֶה שֶׁאוֹמְרִים: "וּבָנָה לָנוּ" דַּיְיקָא "אֶת בֵּית הַבְּחִירָה".
And this is why we say specifically, "And He built for us the Chosen House."
וּבְשַׁבָּת אֲפִילּוּ עוֹבֵד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה כְּדוֹר אֱנוֹשׁ מָחוּל לוֹ, כִּדְאִיתָא בְּשַׁבָּת
And on Shabbos, even one who worships idols like the generation of Enosh is forgiven, as stated in Shabbos
וְזֶה שֶׁאוֹמְרִים: "לְכַפֵּר עַל כָּל עֲוֹנוֹתֵינוּ".
and this is why we say, "to atone for all our iniquities."
וּבְשַׁבָּת זוֹ הַזְּמַן בְּיוֹתֵר, כְּמוֹ שֶׁמּוּבָא
And on this Shabbos it is especially the opportune time, as brought
(תִּיקּוּנֵי זֹהַר תִּיקּוּן י"ט):
(Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 19):
שַׁבָּת הַגָּדוֹל בִּינָה, שַׁבָּת הַקָּטָן מַלְכוּת;
"Shabbos HaGadol is Binah, Shabbos HaKatan is Malchus";
אוֹמְרִים בּוֹ עַד "לְכַפֵּר עַל כָּל עֲוֹנוֹתֵינוּ",
we recite on it until "to atone for all our iniquities,"
שֶׁזּוֹכִין לִבְחִינַת הַדַּעַת וּלְבִנְיַן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ,
for we merit the aspect of Da'as and the building of the Holy Temple,
וּכְשֶׁזּוֹכִין לְשַׁבָּת עִילָּאָה עַל יְדֵי שְׁמִירַת שַׁבָּת, אָז שׁוֹמֵר שַׁבָּת מָחוּל לוֹ.
and when one merits the Supernal Shabbos through observing Shabbos, then one who observes Shabbos is forgiven.

paragraphs.text: Pesachim 117a — "How far does one recite [Hallel at the Seder]? Beis Shammai say: until 'the mother of children is joyful' (Tehillim 113:9); Beis Hillel say: until 'flint into a fountain of water' (114:8). Another baraisa: Beis Shammai say until 'When Israel went forth from Egypt' (114:1); Beis Hillel say until 'Not to us, Hashem' (115:1)." Rashbam (117b): the two versions differ on whether "until" includes the named verse.

paragraphs.text: Shabbos 118a–b — "Whoever delights in the Shabbos is given an inheritance without boundaries, as it says (Yeshayahu 58:14), 'Then you shall delight in Hashem... and I will feed you the inheritance of Yaakov your father': not like Avraham ('Arise, walk the land, its length...'), nor like Yitzchak ('to you and your seed I will give all these lands'), but like Yaakov: 'You shall spread out west, east, north and south.'" Rashi: "without boundaries" means it has no end.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefas Emes, Vayeitzei 5652 — “‘Whoever delights in the Shabbos is given an inheritance without boundaries … the inheritance of Yaakov your father … and you shall spread out westward and eastward.’ It is as written, ‘The land on which you lie’: the Holy One folded the whole Land of Israel beneath him, the root point, the Foundation Stone from which the world is founded. Yaakov merited the place of the foundation, and ‘to you I will give it and to your seed’: every Jew has a share in this gift, and it is fulfilled on Shabbos. Therefore it says of Shabbos, ‘Let no man go out of his place,’ which implies that Shabbos gives each Jew a place. Of this we say, ‘Who spreads the shelter of peace over us … and over Jerusalem.’” Connection: Both read Yaakov's boundless inheritance as Shabbos bringing the holiness of the Land and the Temple to a Jew wherever he is; Sefas Emes adds that Shabbos gives each Jew his own place, rooted in the Foundation Stone.

paragraphs.text: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 48 (85a) — "'And the Children of Israel shall keep the Shabbos, to make the Shabbos' (Shemos 31:16): Shabbos is mentioned twice here, corresponding to the upper and lower Shechinah. What is 'for their generations' (l'dorosam)? Fortunate is he who makes a dwelling (dirah) for them on Shabbos in the two chambers of the heart, and the evil inclination, which is the desecration of Shabbos, is cleared out from there."

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Chanukah 2 — “Through keeping Shabbos properly they are immediately redeemed: although the world is judged by its majority and the Temple is not built, every individual soul that keeps Shabbos properly is fully redeemed. Even though the Temple was not built in his days, his heart becomes a dwelling for the Shechinah and is like the Temple, ‘My holy mountain.’ This is ‘Anyone who has de'ah, it is as if the Temple was built in his days’: one who has merited Da'as, the inner aspect of Kesser, his heart becomes a dwelling for the Shechinah. And the elders' mitzvah was to light Chanukah lights, to make a dedication for the Shechinah's dwelling in the heart.” Connection: Both read Berachos 33a as the heart becoming the Temple through Shabbos; Chanukah 2 makes this the individual's redemption while the Temple stands unbuilt, and extends it to the Chanukah lights.
